slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies to protect your brain
from aging

learning an instrument

spend 15 minutes a day learning an instrument, even badly. music works memory, coordination and attention at once, and few habits challenge the brain so completely.

long walks outside

walk for 30 minutes outside every day, ideally somewhere green. movement and fresh air are two of the simplest things you can do for a brain you want to keep sharp.

daily lessons

spend 5 minutes a day learning something completely new: a moment in history, a scientific idea, a famous artwork. a brain that keeps learning is a brain that keeps building new connections.
slides.texte_sophia:
daily lessons

spend 5 minutes a day learning something completely new: a moment in history, a scientific idea. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and a learning brain keeps building connections.

slides.texte_overlay:
dinner with friends

have one long dinner a week with people you love, phones away. real conversation is one of the most complex things your brain does, and loneliness is one of the worst things for it.

a new route home

take a different route home once a week and find your way without the map. figuring out where you are gives the memory parts of your brain a workout most of us skip.
